lead: Adobe / ADBE — the AI tools will pay
smaller: D-Wave / QBTS — the breakthrough rally goes on
Intel / INTC — the comeback under a new CEO
Dogecoin / DOGE — the joke is the asset
why_lead: ADBE fell 13.85% in the 13 March session and 18.35% over 20 sessions after a record quarter with a dull outlook. Reuters, CNBC and Stocktwits tie the drop to AI monetisation doubts and to retail mood at rock bottom, and no earlier lead covered Adobe. The Tesla lead of 12 March is retired because the draft lead repeated its loyalty essay with the same Business Insider quote and the same political-storm mechanism; Tesla stays only in the section intro as the dominant popular trade.
why_smaller: QBTS: the largest one-session surge among the speculative names in the card (+18.73%), on an upbeat forecast Reuters reported on 13 March [n3158]. The quantum story is the 13 March lead's, so it stays only because the reaction changed: IonQ and Rigetti fell in the same session.

INTC: no earlier retail appearance. A 14.60% session on the CEO appointment and a TSMC foundry-venture report, with attention from trader and headline coverage rather than a retail source; the foundry story rests on sources, not a signed deal.

DOGE: the 13 March trivia-prize trade is retired. The changed story is the 13 March New York memecoin suspension, which does not name Dogecoin, and Robinhood's new listings the same day, a regulatory and listing change.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla (TSLA, -28.48% over 20 sessions): the 12 March lead already told the loyalty and political-storm story with the same Business Insider quote, Ron Baron and pension points; the 13 March CNBC and JPMorgan items are a dated attention note, not a new lead.

Oklo (OKLO, -55.96% over 20 sessions): the Big Tech nuclear catalyst is the same 12 March item used in the 13 March smaller trade; the new Reuters CERAweek piece is a changed story, but the rest of the evidence repeats, so it was not kept as a smaller trade.
Robinhood (HOOD, -35.58% over 20 sessions): a lead on 11 March; the 13 March Cramer call and PENGU listing are new, but a second lead on the same name would repeat an earlier lead.
SoFi (SOFI, -22.88% over 20 sessions): the 13 March Blue Owl loan deal is new, but the credit-fear backdrop was already used as peer context in the 11 March lead.
Rheinmetall (RHM.DE, +70.15% over 20 sessions): a lead on 5 and 10 March and a smaller trade on 12 and 13 March; the market-value overtaking of Volkswagen is not a new story.
Rocket Lab (RKLB, -36.39% over 20 sessions): the 2X fund launch and the Mynaric deal are new since the 11 March smaller trade, but the fund's own price is not in the card.
Hims & Hers (HIMS, -31.94% over 20 sessions): the weight-loss drug selloff is a sector move with no retail-attention item of its own.
